parts.context: A woman books tickets at a theatre box office.

transcript.text: Good morning, Royal Theatre box office. How can I help?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Hello. I'd like to book tickets for The Winter Garden, please. I heard it's wonderful.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: It certainly is. The reviews have been fantastic, and the cast is excellent.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: I'm so pleased. I've wanted to see it ever since it opened.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: It's very popular. Which date are you thinking of?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Saturday the tenth of May, if possible.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: I'm sorry, Saturday is sold out. We have some seats on Friday the ninth of May. Would that suit you?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Yes, Friday would be fine. We could go straight after work.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Wonderful. It's a good time for the show, since the weather will probably be pleasant.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Yes, we're hoping to have dinner nearby first.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Good. How many tickets do you need?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Four. Myself, my husband and my parents.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Four tickets. And your name, please?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Ruth Mackenzie. That's M-A-C-K-E-N-Z-I-E.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Thank you, Mrs Mackenzie. You'll also receive a confirmation by email, so please check that it arrives.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Of course. It's the email I use for my bank, so I look at it every day.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Thank you, Mrs Mackenzie. Do you prefer to sit in the stalls or the circle?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: What's the difference in price?
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Let me give you the prices. The stalls are twenty-eight pounds, the circle is twenty-two pounds, and the balcony is fifteen pounds. Students can buy a ticket for ten pounds in any part of the theatre.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: My parents are both over seventy. Is there a discount?
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Yes, senior citizens receive a discount of twenty percent on the stalls and circle tickets, though not on the balcony.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Then I think we'll take the circle. Is there a seat in row F?
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: It's a good choice. The circle has a clear view of the whole stage, and it's not too far from the actors.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: That's what my husband likes. He doesn't enjoy sitting too close.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Row F is available, yes. I can give you four seats together. Shall I book those?
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Please. And can I collect the tickets at the theatre?
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Yes, you can collect them at the box office up to thirty minutes before the show. You just need to show a photo ID and the card you paid with.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: My parents don't like walking far, so I'll ask them to meet us at the entrance.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: That sounds wise. There are also chairs in the foyer if they arrive early.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Thank you. What time does the show start?
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: The curtain goes up at seven thirty, but the doors open an hour earlier, so you can have a drink in the bar first.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: There's a good restaurant opposite the theatre if you need a recommendation.
transcript.speaker: BEN

transcript.text: Thank you, we'll try it. Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: RUTH

transcript.text: Goodbye, Mrs Mackenzie.
transcript.speaker: BEN
